learning: Controller tests so far (base_speed 1.15, kd 0.4, kd 0.2) all lowered the score, so kd 0.3 and base_speed 1.3 are the supported values. Line-loss handling is the untested lever. If line_loss_events is still about 1 per run here, the next single change should be line_loss handling.
notes: Reference robot: the iteration 1 geometry and controller exactly, with kd at its best-measured value of 0.3. Any change from 69.32 in later iterations can be attributed to the single change made then.
rationale: Evidence: the iteration 1 controller on this geometry (base_speed 1.3, kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, last_direction, weights -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) scored 69.3241 in iterations 1, 4 and 6, so it is reproducible. Every controller change tested on it lowered the score: base_speed 1.15 gave 61.77 (iteration 7, oval line loss rose to 1.45), kd 0.4 gave 56.44 (iteration 8, oscillation rose to about 0.14), and kd 0.2 gave 63.59 (iteration 9). That puts kd 0.3 at a local optimum among the values tested. Every geometry change tested also lowered the score: 16 mm footprint 54.45, y = 0.03 m 59.64, span ±0.04 m 52.47. Line loss has stayed at about 1 per run (1.0 to 1.65) under every design, and steering oscillation (0.07 to 0.15) is not limiting. I therefore package the best-measured robot exactly, with the geometry and controller unchanged, so the race gives a known-good score and a clean reference. Sign check: positive x (left) carries a positive weight, so a line on the left steers left, as the contract requires. Expected result: a score near 69.3 with line loss about 1 per run. This is a prediction from repeated measurement, not a new outcome. The one lever not yet tested is line-loss handling (search_left or search_right in place of last_direction), which I leave for a later single-variable test because changing it now would move the reference.
